Why Nepali Students Choose to Study in the UK from Nepal

Thousands of Nepali students dream of studying in the UK every year, and for good reasons. The United Kingdom remains one of the most prestigious destinations for higher education, offering world-class universities, diverse programs, and excellent career opportunities for international students.

When you decide to study in the UK from Nepal, you’re investing in a qualification recognized globally, opening doors to international career prospects and personal growth. UK universities consistently rank among the top institutions worldwide, with institutions like Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial College London, and the University of Edinburgh leading global rankings.
Benefits of Studying in the UK for Nepali Students
UK degrees are respected worldwide, with rigorous quality standards maintained by independent bodies.
Undergraduate degrees typically last three years, and master’s programs one year, saving you time and money compared to other countries.
International students can work up to 20 hours per week during term time and full-time during holidays.
The Graduate Route lets bachelor's and master's graduates stay for 18 months after their degree. PhD graduates get 3 years.
The UK hosts students from over 200 countries, creating a rich multicultural environment.
UK universities invest heavily in research and innovation, providing excellent facilities and funding.

Admission Requirements to Study in the UK from Nepal
To successfully study in the UK from Nepal, you’ll need to meet specific admission criteria:
Completion of 10+2 or A-levels with good grades
Some universities accept SEE (Grade 10) plus 2 years of further education
Bachelor’s degree (16 years of education) with minimum 55-60%
Relevant work experience may strengthen your application
Alternative options like medium of instruction letters or university English tests may be accepted by some institutions.

Student Life When You Study in the UK from Nepal
Life in the UK offers Nepali students an enriching experience beyond academics.
The UK hosts a thriving Nepali community with associations, cultural events, and festivals. Cities like London, Birmingham, Manchester, and Reading have active Nepali student networks.

International students can work up to 20 hours weekly during term time and full-time during holidays. Common part-time jobs include retail, hospitality, tutoring, and campus jobs, with pay typically £10-£12 per hour.
Shared houses or flats (£80-200/week per person)
International students pay the Immigration Health Surcharge and can access NHS services. Registration with a GP is recommended upon arrival.

Frequently Asked Questions About Studying in the UK from Nepal
How much does it cost to study in the UK from Nepal?
Total annual costs range from £15,000 to £50,000, including tuition and living expenses, depending on the course and location.
Can I work while studying in the UK?
Yes, Student visa holders at degree level can work up to 20 hours per week during term and full-time during holidays.
What is the visa success rate for Nepali students?
With proper documentation and guidance from Admizz Education, the success rate is over 95%.
How long can I stay in the UK after completing my studies?
The Graduate Route lets bachelor's and master's graduates stay for 18 months after their degree. PhD graduates get 3 years.
Do I need to show financial proof?
Yes, you must demonstrate the ability to pay the first year’s tuition plus 9 months of living costs.
Which intake is better – September or January?The
September (Fall) intake has more course options and scholarship opportunities, but the January intake offers faster enrollment.
Only students on postgraduate research courses (such as a PhD) can bring dependants. Students on taught master's courses cannot, and the visa fee and financial requirements apply to each dependant.
